bullets.title: Oil surges to $90+ WTI / ~$100 Brent on Houthi tanker attacks; inflation and rate hike fears spike
bullets.body: Brent crude approached $100/bbl (+5%) and WTI crossed $90 for the first time since June 11 after Iran-backed Houthis struck Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea; Murban futures spiked 26% to $112.56/bbl. The oil shock is reigniting inflation fears globally, with July rate hike odds climbing to 38% (vs near-zero prior) and analysts flagging $100 oil as a risk-off threshold. Hormuz transits have dropped ~75%; an analyst assigns 2/3 odds Trump chooses diplomacy over military escalation.

bullets.title: Global yields spike to cycle highs; 10Y at 4.69%, 2Y at 4.32%; technical target 4.8%
bullets.body: US 10-year yields hit a year-to-date high of 4.69% and 2-year yields reached 4.32%, driven by oil-driven inflation fears and anticipated sovereign debt supply. Germany's 10Y hit 3.2% (15-year high) and UK 5Y reached 5.10%. Technical analysis points to 4.8% as next resistance for the 10Y. Multiple sources identify 4.7% on the 10Y and $100 oil as the market's pain threshold that could trigger risk-off.

bullets.title: Market pricing in Fed rate HIKE by December; jobless claims hit 57-year low at 187k
bullets.body: Futures markets are pricing at least one Fed rate hike by December following a strong jobless claims print of 187k (vs 211k expected), the lowest since 1969. M2, bank loans, and federal outlays are all accelerating, boosting nominal growth and putting upward pressure on yields. Fed sentiment models show FOMC members increasingly concerned about inflation passthrough from oil.

bullets.title: ECB on track for September rate hike; risks skewed to further hikes if oil stays elevated
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects ECB to hike in September, noting some governors considered hiking at the July meeting. Core inflation is expected to run above 2% target through 1H27. Additional hikes are possible if oil stays above $75/bbl and European gas above €50/MWh; European gas prices are up 52% month-to-date.

bullets.title: VIX surges to 19.79 (+18.9%); asset manager VIX futures positioning at 1st percentile — extreme complacency now being tested
bullets.body: VIX rose 18.9% to 19.79 with the S&P 500 at 7,382.78 (+1.6% per the options note context). Asset managers' VIX futures positioning has fallen to the 1st percentile, a historically extreme complacency reading now being stress-tested by geopolitical and macro headwinds. Unusual options volume spiked across multiple names (ACN 230% above avg, DECK 300% above avg).

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex race accelerates: Google raises FY26 to $195-205B, FY27 expected ~$300B; sector FCF turns negative
bullets.body: Google raised FY26 capex guidance 8% to $195-205B and management signaled a significant FY27 step-up (consensus floor ~$263B, potentially toward $300B). Google printed its first-ever negative free cash flow quarter (-$5.86B). Hyperscaler aggregate 2027 capex survey implies a median of ~$1.1T across all players. OpenAI raised its own capex projection from $600B to $750B through 2030. Markets are increasingly questioning ROIC given FCF deterioration.

bullets.title: AI capex validates infrastructure beneficiaries: optical, memory, power — but raises margin risk for hyperscalers
bullets.body: Google's Cloud revenue surged 82% YoY with 36% EBIT margin and $514B backlog, validating AI demand. Google is also bridging to third-party compute capacity (benefiting SPCX/rented GPU capacity) while internal capacity builds. AVGO, LITE, CLS, MU, SNDK, STX/WDC, NVDA, AMD, and GLW identified as hyperscaler capex beneficiaries. Morgan Stanley recommends buying the dip in memory stocks. DRAM cycle inflection risk is rising, with 85% gross margins attracting simultaneous capacity additions from Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, and Chinese state-subsidized producers.

bullets.title: Mag7 bifurcates: AI infrastructure winners (NOW +6%) vs. capex/margin losers (TSLA -6%, GOOGL -4%)
bullets.body: Pre-market showed sharp divergence within mega-cap tech: ServiceNow surged ~6% on a strong cRPO beat, while TSLA fell 6%+ on margin collapse and GOOGL fell ~4-5% despite a Cloud beat, as rising capex and negative FCF spooked investors. INFY dropped 5% on weak bookings, STM fell 16% on guidance, and TMUS fell 8% on soft 3Q guidance. The Hedgeye '#Bag7' framework flags bearish TRADE/TREND signals on GOOGL, TSLA, MSFT, AMZN, and META, with AAPL as the lone bullish holdout.

bullets.title: ISM Manufacturing tracking 53.8 in July; Kansas City Fed shows moderation but expansion intact
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's ISM PMI nowcast is tracking at 53.8 for July, up from 53.3 in June, as the Kansas City Fed survey showed moderating but still-expansionary production and new orders. Both prices paid and prices received decelerated meaningfully in the KC survey, offering some relief on input inflation. US Earnings Revision Index remains positive but below its May peak.

bullets.title: Euro area consumer confidence beats in July; JPM raises Q3 household spending nowcast to 1.3%ar
bullets.body: Flash EC consumer confidence rose 1.7pts in July, beating consensus and JPM's unchanged call. Though still 1.3 standard deviations below the long-run average, confidence has retraced roughly half its post-conflict decline. JPM raised its Q3 euro area household spending nowcast to 1.3%ar from 0.75%ar, implying upside risk, though elevated fuel prices remain a threat.

bullets.title: Bond market weakness supply-driven, not a confidence-in-Fed crisis — curve not steepening
bullets.body: One analyst argues the current bond weakness is driven by demand growth holding up and anticipated debt supply rising, not a loss of confidence in Fed inflation management. The yield curve is not steepening, and 5Y5Y CPI forward inflation expectations have not moved materially. Bond vigilantes are reasserting, with sovereigns (including the US) being forced to offer larger premiums to attract buyers competing against debt-hungry hyperscalers.

bullets.title: Week ahead: Fed decision July 29, Mag7 earnings (META, MSFT, AAPL, AMZN) July 28-30, key macro data
bullets.body: The upcoming week is packed with catalysts: Fed decision on July 29 (expected on hold, but hawkish tone anticipated with 1-2 dissents and ~38% July hike odds), plus Mag7 earnings from META, MSFT, AAPL, and AMZN reporting July 29-30. Key macro releases include Durable Goods, ADP, PCE, GDP, and Employment data. BOE decides July 30, BOJ July 31.

bullets.title: Mortgage applications rise 1.9% but 30-year rate climbs to 6.7%, highest since Aug 2023; consumer debt stress elevated
bullets.body: MBA mortgage applications rose 1.9% for the week ended July 17 vs. -2.7% prior, but the 30-year rate increased to 6.7%, the highest since August 2023. Separately, 25%+ of US working-age adults who used credit cards for groceries couldn't repay their bills in full, signaling elevated lower-income consumer stress.

bullets.title: China credit-fiscal impulse signals risk of negative growth surprises; CXMT memory IPO targets global leaders
bullets.body: BCA Research notes China's combined credit and fiscal impulse — the strongest leading indicator of activity — is signaling increased risk of negative growth surprises ahead. Separately, ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) IPO launches July 27 on Shanghai STAR Market raising $8.5B to compete in memory, targeting the three companies controlling 90% of the global market (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron).

bullets.title: UAE to import high-end AI chips 'very soon'; UAE $1.4T US investment pledge ahead of schedule
bullets.body: The UAE announced it will import high-end AI chips from the US 'very soon,' opening a new geopolitical channel for US semiconductor exports. The UAE also stated its $1.4T US investment pledge is tracking ahead of schedule. These announcements represent a potential demand catalyst for NVDA, INTC, and AMD.

bullets.title: AI-disruption 'loser' basket (GSTMTAIR) recovered ~15% off YTD lows; Goldman sees opportunity to revisit short thesis
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs notes its AI-disruption-exposed basket (GSTMTAIR) recovered ~15% from YTD lows following the recent relief rally and is now outperforming the S&P ex-AI index (SPXXAI) off those lows. Goldman is hosting a webinar to revisit the short thesis on AI-disrupted companies, covering momentum drivers, trading flows, hedging, and basket positioning.

bullets.title: 60% of active mutual fund Q2 holdings were AI plays; non-AI funds face underperformance/redemption risk
bullets.body: 60% of active mutual fund holdings at end of Q2 were AI-related positions. Funds not positioned in AI face risk of massive underperformance and subsequent redemptions, creating potential forced-buying feedback loop in AI names regardless of fundamentals.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 up 19.3% YTD, outperforming S&P 500 by 9.7%; early 2Q small-cap earnings tracking +5.2% above expectations
bullets.body: Russell 2000 is outperforming S&P 500 by 9.7% YTD despite falling 0.9% on July 22. Of the 99 Russell 2000 companies (8% of market cap) that have reported Q2, aggregate earnings are running 5.2% above expectations (12.6% ex-financials), suggesting small-cap earnings quality is holding up early in the season.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex driving record credit issuance: MIS-rated volume exceeded $2T for second consecutive quarter
bullets.body: Moody's reported MIS-rated issuance exceeded $2T for the second consecutive quarter in 2Q26, up ~20% YTD, with hyperscaler and data center/AI capex visible across CFG (+35%), PPIF (+52%), and FIG (+25%) transactional revenues. Moody's now forecasts ~$800B in hyperscaler capex in 2026, up from ~$700B in April. JPM believes MIS revenue guidance of +HSD% is conservative, as at least one hyperscaler has not yet tapped credit markets for AI capex.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk: EU sanctions 50+ Russian military entities; Houthi maritime blockade threat targets Saudi Arabia
bullets.body: The EU added 50+ military-industrial entities to sanctions lists (including drone manufacturers) and targeted 100+ banks, crypto operators, and 40 shadow fleet vessels. Houthis are threatening a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and claiming strikes on Saudi tankers, with EU's Kallas calling it a 'dangerous escalation.' Trump is signaling potential restart of Yemen bombing.
